subject: Greenbridge: Instrumentation audit + customer dashboard access for uptime/latency SLOs
messages:

To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@greenbridge.ai>, Greenbridge Procurement <procurement@greenbridge.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Greenbridge: Instrumentation audit + customer dashboard access for uptime/latency SLOs

Hi Sara / procurement team,

Thanks for sending over the questionnaire. I pulled together a compact measurement matrix (attached) that maps our internal telemetry to the SLO fields on your template. High level: we currently publish availability and latency SLOs (availability measured as successful completion within a configurable request timeout, latency reported as p50/p95/p99 for generation time).

Next steps I suggest:
- I can provision read-only Grafana access to the specific dashboards you asked for (token-level latency/cost and per-route availability).
- Vivek can outline the exact measurement windows and exclusion rules we use for maintenance and model rollouts.
- If you have any required audit window (e.g., 90 vs 365 days), flag that and we can scope retention/exports.

Attachments: redwood_slo_measurement_matrix.xlsx (mapping + definitions).

Would you prefer a short walkthrough tomorrow (15–20m) to confirm the dashboards? If so, propose two slots and we’ll lock one.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Greenbridge: Instrumentation audit + customer dashboard access for uptime/latency SLOs

Tessa — thanks, got the matrix and skimmed it. Helpful. Two quick clarifications before we schedule: 

1) When you say "latency reported as p50/p95/p99", do you compute those at the request level across all regions or per-region? We need per-region p99 for our runbook.
2) For availability, do you use calendar-month windows or rolling 30d windows? Procurement wants the exact definition written into the SLO clause.

Also please confirm whether we can get a CSV export of raw request samples for audit purposes (Redwood can redact user content, of course). If you can send the read-only Grafana invite instructions as an attachment, that will help our ops team.

Sara Lim
Head of Engineering Operations, Greenbridge Analytics

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@greenbridge.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Greenbridge: Instrumentation audit + customer dashboard access for uptime/latency SLOs

Hi Sara / Tessa / Laura,

Thanks for the questions — happy to be explicit. Summary of our measurement and access approach (short):

- Measurement windows: Primary SLOs are computed on a rolling 30-day window for internal monitoring and a calendar-month window for contractual reporting. Both are available in exports; the contractual clause can reference the calendar-month definition if you prefer.

- Availability definition: A request counts as successful if the model returns a final response within the configured request timeout (default 60s for hosted API). Timeouts, client disconnects, and 5xx backend errors are treated as failures. Partial responses (stream started but not completed) are counted as failures for availability but latency is reported separately.

- Latency metrics: We compute per-request generation time and publish p50/p95/p99 per-region and per-model-route. By default we aggregate at the region level (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) and provide filterable views in Grafana.

- Exclusions and maintenance: Scheduled maintenance windows are excluded if published through our Maintenance API and agreed in advance. For model rollouts (new weights/quantization), we provide a 72-hour transient window; measurable regressions during that window are flagged and subject to canary rollback policy rather than SLA penalties. For unplanned incidents, we follow our incident classification and remediation timelines; exceptions may be requested via our SLO Exception form (linked below).

- Monitoring & tooling: Metrics are exported from the runtime to Prometheus, aggregated into Grafana dashboards (read-only links available). Alerting is managed in PagerDuty (internal) and can be bridged to your existing on-call via webhooks or Opsgenie. Long-term metric retention (beyond 90 days) is available as an enterprise add-on.

- Audit/export: We can provide CSV exports of metric buckets and sampled request metadata (timestamp, region, route, latency_ms, status_code) with PII redaction. Exports are delivered via a secure GCS transfer; retention and frequency are configurable in the contract.

Links and attachments: I've attached a step-by-step for provisioning Grafana read-only accounts and a short diagram showing where metrics live (production-uptime-7d.png). Also see: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bSLOPlaybook (SLO playbook).

If useful, I can formalize the wording for a contract clause describing the rolling vs calendar windows and the exception process.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@greenbridge.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenbridge Procurement <procurement@greenbridge.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Greenbridge: Instrumentation audit + customer dashboard access for uptime/latency SLOs

Vivek — super helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups so procurement can close the thread: 

- The per-region p99 is a hard requirement; please include a sample CSV export with per-region p99 for the last 3 months when you send the contract wording.
- For exception handling: we need a 5-business-day SLA on reviewing SLO exception requests and a clear approval path (who signs off for model-rollout exceptions versus infrastructure outages). Can you propose a sign-off matrix?
- For model rollout transient windows: can we get a notification hook (webhook or email) when a canary rollout starts so our on-call can expect transient noise?

We accepted your proposed walkthrough — Tuesday 2026-06-23 at 10:00am PT works for our ops and procurement people. Please send calendar invite and Grafana read-only invite instructions (the .txt you attached earlier).

Thanks — Sara
